definition: In this packet, developmental schedules refers to the Gesell Developmental Schedules, a child development assessment that provides scores in areas such as gross motor functioning. It is used to relate aspects of development to clinical features in children.

reasons: The packet supports that GDS stands for Gesell Developmental Schedules and that gross motor scores were used in an ASD correlation analysis, but it does not support the broader claim that it is a child development assessment in general clinical use.

The statement that it is used to relate aspects of development to clinical features in children overgeneralizes a single study correlation; the packet does not establish this as the instrument’s purpose or a current diagnostic use.
The definition is not fully supported by the packet as written, because it adds interpretive claims about what developmental schedules are used for beyond the source text.

The packet only mentions correlations between “Gesell Developmental Schedules (GDS) gross motor scores” and clinical features in an ASD group; it does not explicitly state the general purpose that developmental schedules are “used to relate aspects of development to clinical features in children.”
